This part of the completion code is pretty problematic IMO. It basically calls any native method that is marked as `const` when the arguments in the code are known at compile time.

I feel like it completely disregards the fact, that `const` methods can still cause side effects (e.g. a crash).

We should probably just remove it completely. As far as I know, there are very few cases were this approach would actually yield better results than just the static type hint (e.g. `Resource.duplicate()`), those could just be hard coded special cases.

@Yanxiyimengya What is happening is the code complete is calling all the exposed RenderingServer functions that are marked with `const`. For some reason `create_local_rendering_device()` is marked as const despite it creating a new RenderingDevice. 

`create_local_rendering_device()` returns a pointer to the RenderingDevice. Which means that it needs to be freed manually. But of course, it is never freed, because the code complete system just throws the return value away immediately. 

Therefore, every time code complete is called, it leaks an entire RenderingDevice. 

To fix this we need to ensure that `create_local_rendering_device()` is never called by code complete. I am testing right now to see if simply removing the `const` label from `create_local_rendering_device()` is viable

@clayjohn if your solution doesn't work and you can't fix it without breaking the ABI, the most likely solution would be to use some sort of annotation.

In C++ terms create_local_rendering_device() is [not pure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pure_function). It is common to confuse const with pure. Pure functions must not modify external state, const can.

Compilers use extensions to annotate pure functions such as sin(), cos(), etc. They also use other annotations such as malloc to indicate the function is malloc (it has side effects, but the returned pointer is not aliased to anything).

In other words:

```cpp
#define gd_pure

RenderingDevice *create_local_rendering_device() const gd_pure;
```

**Edit:** I realize my suggestion would lead to rewriting entire headers just to add `gd_pure`. In that case it may be better to use `gd_nonpure`. However the advantage of using gd_pure is that we can actually use compiler extensions too and get compiler errors:


```cpp
#define gd_pure __attribute__((pure))
#define gd_pure __attribute__((const)) // This extension is even more strict than pure. See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29117836/attribute-const-vs-attribute-pure-in-gnu-c
```

> code complete is calling all the exposed RenderingServer functions

It doesn't call all exposed functions. But as soon as a function is somehow relevant to the type detection e.g. by being the initializer of a variable for which properties should be listed.
